thread:
oncall-bot: ALERT: Elevated 502/504 error rate detected for API gateway (edge-us-west-2) — threshold breached at 07:34:25 UTC. Error-rate: 12% (5m). Paging oncall. severity: high :rotating_light:

ingress-proxy-bot: Proxy pool "edge-usw2-pool-3" reporting spike. Sample trace ids: 01a3.., 01a4.., upstream timeouts present. Logs batched to #log-aggregation -> https://grafana.internal/redwood/ingress?from=now-10m&to=now

maria: ack. I see 502 and 504 mix in dashboard. 95th latency up to 2.1s, error rate uptick aligned with a surge from a specific CIDR block. Trying to isolate if it's upstream overload or proxy resource exhaustion.

kevin: oncall here, acked pager. quick checklist: (1) confirm ingress pod health (2) check node CPU/NET (3) check upstream connection pool exhaustion (4) fallback routing policy. I'll start with pod health.

kevin: running checks:
```
kubectl get pods -n ingress -o wide
NAME                             READY  STATUS   RESTARTS  AGE
edge-proxy-5c9f8d7d7f-2k9pz     2/2    Running  3         12d
edge-proxy-5c9f8d7d7f-7l2qm     2/2    Running  0         3h
edge-proxy-5c9f8d7d7f-9m4tx     0/2    CrashLoopBackOff  5   15m
```
Errors in the crashing pod show `connect: connection reset by peer` to upstreams.

ops-sre: HPA metrics show CPU at ~85% across pool-3. Node network tx spikes too. Autoscaler didn't spin up extra nodes yet — quota is at limit for the AZ.

jess: I'm jumping in to take over triage (oncall handoff). @kevin please annotate if you want me to continue. Initial mitigation suggestions: (a) shift traffic from pool-3 to pool-1/2 via routing weight change, (b) temporarily increase upstream timeouts from 30s -> 60s to reduce 504s caused by slow backends, (c) add a short per-IP rate cap to limit noisy clients.

maria: shifting weights now to reduce pressure on pool-3. Patching routing config:
```
PATCH /routing/policies/edge-weight
{"edge-usw2":{"pool-1":45, "pool-2":45, "pool-3":10}}
```
Status: 202 accepted.

maria: also enabling on-the-fly timeout bump for edge proxies to 60s. Applying config:
```
edge.proxy.timeout.upstream=60s
```
Deployed to pool-1/2/3, rolling restart for pool-3 pods started to pick up new setting.

kevin: good. also applied a temporary rate-limit rule:
```
rate_limit: requests_per_minute: 600 per_ip
```
This is targeted to suspect CIDR ranges only.

cs-bot: Customer impact summary (automated): ~3.4% of active API keys experiencing increased 5xx errors (last 10m). Top affected customers: acme-inc (0.9% of total requests), beta-staging (0.6%), partner-alpha (0.4%). CS alerted for any SLA customers impacted.

ingress-proxy-bot: After weight change + timeout bump, error rate trending down: 5xx = 4.2% -> 1.8% over 6m. 504s dropped faster than 502s.

jess: Observed root cause hypothesis: sudden increase in long-polling requests from a noisy client plus AZ quota preventing autoscaler from adding nodes; upstream pools hit connection limits causing resets (502) and timeouts (504). Mitigations performed: routing weight shift, upstream timeout increase, per-ip caps.

kevin: agree with hypothesis. Next immediate step: we need to open a quota request for the AZ to allow capacity to scale (ops ticket CREATED-4312), and follow-up to add circuit-breaker for long-tail upstream slow responses.

maria: rolling restart of the CrashLoopBackOff pod completed and it's now Ready 2/2. No further restarts.

ops-sre: node autoscaler quota increased (provision pending). Observed connection pool free slots recovered after shifting traffic.

jess: moving to monitoring-only; will handoff to next oncall in 30m. If any regression, recreate the thread and tag @escalations.

kevin: quick post-impact numbers for incident record: peak 5xx 12% at 07:34 UTC, sustained 5xx 1.5% after mitigations, ~3.4% of API keys touched, estimated customer-facing errors ~0.7% of total requests persisted for 10m. No data loss, no S3 or DB correlated errors.

maria: filing a short incident report and linking graphs. Next steps: postmortem, quota change tracking, add HPA override for surge windows, and add rate-limit rule to block the noisy CIDR permanently if abuse persists.

cs-bot: Notified customer success for the three most impacted customers.

jess: thanks team. closing active mitigations, will convert to follow-up Epic for circuit-breaker and autoscaler quota work. :white_check_mark:
